spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work comes from treating the prime-counting function and the ordered primes as generalized-inverse descriptions. At prime arguments the identity π(p_n)=n transfers the counting asymptotic to p_n, while for arbitrary x the bracket p_n≤x<p_{n+1} and the asymptotic agreement of adjacent prime scales transfer it back.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The span proves the equivalence of π(x)∼x/log x and p_n∼n log n. In the forward direction, the counting asymptotic gives log π(x)/log x→1 and hence π(x)log π(x)/x→1; setting x=p_n and using π(p_n)=n yields p_n∼n log n. Conversely, choosing n by p_n≤x<p_{n+1}, the assumed nth-prime asymptotic makes both endpoints asymptotic to n log n, so x∼n log n; with y=π(x)=n and log x∼log y, this gives y∼x/log x.
directed.conceptual_reading: A monotone counting function and its generalized inverse carry the same leading asymptotic once the logarithmic factor is shown stable under the change of variables. The proof separates an exact inverse relation at jump points from a squeeze argument between jumps.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the exact identity π(p_n)=n, the interval p_n≤x<p_{n+1}, and the logarithmic comparison log π(x)/log x→1. Together they move between the continuous-variable counting representation and the discrete enumeration representation without estimating individual prime gaps.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument establishes only leading asymptotic equivalence, with no error term or rate. It relies on monotone indexing and on adjacent scales (n+1)log(n+1) and n log n being asymptotically equal; it does not by itself transfer sharper remainders. The first displayed counting-function symbol is OCR-rendered as τ.
directed.uncertainty: The surrounding equations identify the OCR τ in (1) as the prime-counting function π, but the supplied text span alone does not verify the glyph against the scan. No missing formula has been reconstructed.
